title: Pakistan Releases Official 'Marka-e-Haq' Anniversary Documentary — Day Two of Competing Commemorations
detail: Pakistan's state broadcaster Radio Pakistan announced on May 8, 2026 the release of a special official documentary marking the first anniversary of Marka-e-Haq — Pakistan's name for the May 7–10, 2025 conflict with India. The documentary, produced with ISPR participation, highlights Pakistan's military defense capabilities, the performance of the Pakistan Air Force and Army during the May 2025 confrontation, and Pakistan's intelligence apparatus. The release forms part of Pakistan's multi-day coordinated anniversary information operation: the May 5 Corps Commanders' Conference statement, the May 6 Marka-e-Haq book launch, the 'Tu Yaad Rakhein' patriotic promo, the May 7 DG ISPR tri-service press conference, and culminating with planned May 10 ceremonies marking the ceasefire anniversary. The documentary institutionalizes Pakistan's victory narrative at the one-year mark, appearing the day after PM Modi's India-side commemoration and IAF strike footage release. The combined ISPR information campaign — spanning five consecutive days — represents Pakistan's most sustained state-directed military anniversary communications effort since the 1999 Kargil War. The bilateral standoff remains frozen: airspace closed to each other until May 24, Indus Waters Treaty suspended, all direct trade halted, no ambassadors exchanged.

media.caption: Pakistan state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reports release of official Marka-e-Haq anniversary documentary — Day 2 of national commemorations (May 8, 2026)

title: India Media Reports: Chinese AVIC Engineers Acknowledged On-Ground Technical Support to Pakistan During May 2025 Conflict — Claim Not Independently Verified
detail: Indian media outlet Madhyama Online reported on May 8, 2026 that engineers from China's Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC) publicly acknowledged providing on-ground technical support to Pakistan during the May 7–10, 2025 Operation Sindoor/Marka-e-Haq conflict. If accurate, this would represent a significant public confirmation of China's direct operational involvement in the India-Pakistan confrontation — going beyond Pakistan's previously acknowledged use of Chinese-supplied weapon platforms (J-10C jets, PL-15 beyond-visual-range missiles, JF-17 Block III fighters) to confirm active Chinese engineering personnel presence during combat operations. Indian analysts assessed the reported acknowledgment as consistent with longstanding assessments that Chinese technical personnel were embedded with Pakistan Air Force units, particularly in maintaining the J-10C fleet that reportedly performed a significant role in the aerial engagement. China has maintained strategic ambiguity about its direct operational involvement. The report comes as the anniversary window closes and both sides continue competing narratives about the May 2025 conflict's outcome. The claim originates from a single Indian regional outlet (Madhyama Online, Tier 3) and had not been corroborated by Tier 1 sources or major international news organizations (Reuters, AP, BBC) as of May 9, 2026. Confidence is low pending corroboration.

media.caption: Report: Chinese AVIC engineers acknowledged on-ground technical support to Pakistan during May 2025 conflict — from single Indian outlet, unverified by major outlets (May 8, 2026)
